lines.sr1: Serial transmission sends one bit at a time, over a single wire.
lines.sr2: It works over long distances and arrives fully synchronised, but at a slower rate.
lines.pl1: Parallel transmission sends several bits, usually one byte, over several wires at the same time.
lines.pl2: It works well over short distances, like the circuits inside a computer, where high speed is essential.
lines.pb1: Over long distances, parallel data suffers from skew: bits arrive at slightly different times, or even out of order.
lines.pb2: Crosstalk between the wires also causes interference if the cable is too long.
lines.us1: The universal serial bus, or U S B, sends data serially.
lines.us2: Its advantages include a standard connector, devices detected automatically, power supplied to devices, and backwards compatibility.
lines.us3: Its disadvantages include a limited cable length, and a slower speed than some other connections.
lines.outro: Serial for distance, parallel for short, fast links. And U S B is serial.
